item.title: Why Japan’s Takaichi cannot afford to lose another minister
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is standing by her education minister amid a widening financial scandal, with analysts saying she intends to “ride out the storm” because losing another cabinet member could seriously undermine her leadership. In a worst-case scenario, they warn, the media could sense political blood in the water and an emboldened opposition could put more of her cabinet under the microscope, triggering a “domino effect” of firings or resignations. item.title: Chinese group to develop 10 smart city sites in Indonesia under US$50 billion deal
item.description: A Chinese consortium has reached an initial agreement with Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund to develop 10 smart city sites in the Southeast Asian country, part of a package of two-way deals, the Indonesian side said. An entity under the fund Danantara signed the US$50 billion memorandum of understanding to develop smart cities across the archipelago of 288 million people. item.title: ‘Companions on the same path’: 1 year on, Tai Po fire survivors lean on one another
item.description: A year after Hong Kong’s deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court, Chu Ho-chuen, who lost his 76-year-old father in the tragedy, has formed a new bond with other bereaved families – one that has offered them solace. item.title: Why Russian bombers at South Korea’s doorstep raise stakes for US-led alliances
